subject: Kim Hammer
plainEnglishSummary: In the 2021 regular session Kim Hammer primary-sponsored a six-bill cluster that together reset Arkansas election administration toward tighter poll-site enforcement, county-level control of precincts and vote centers, reduced public access to certain voted-ballot records, revised county election-board governance, stricter absentee handling, and a formal election-law complaint hotline. All six bills enrolled (Acts 727–729, 973–974, 1051). The package is the earliest documented 'integrity architecture' in the KH-0B set and foreshadows 2023 enforcement/equipment emphasis and 2025 petition-process restrictions.
narrativeArc: 2021 establishes enforcement-first posture (SB486 misdemeanors, SB644 hotline) before later-session petition fights.
County administration is centralized in statute early (SB487 precincts/sites; SB582 election boards)—not a 2025 discovery.
Transparency rhetoric splits: public inspection narrows for voted ballots (SB488) while compliance duties expand for counties.
Absentee process is tightened in-session (SB643) before 2023 drop-box and method debates Hammer co-sponsors.
Governance of county election commissioners is modified (SB582), creating a through-line to 2023 SB292 compensation/duties changes.
By 2025 the same sponsor moves friction to initiative/refendum canvassing—continuity is procedural control, not a single-year pivot.
Kelly contrast: Secretary of State as implementation partner for counties vs. legislator stacking unfunded mandates.

strategicBriefing.howToMessage: Frame the 2021 package as a deliberate architecture—not a one-year reaction: enforcement at the polls, county operational control, narrowed public inspection of ballots, absentee tightening, and a statewide complaint hotline. Lead with county clerks and election commissioners who must implement layered rules without added state support.
strategicBriefing.debateImpact: Shifts debate from abstract 'integrity' to who bears compliance cost. Hammer can claim prevention; Kelly can rebut with operational burden and voter-service consequences without alleging fraud.
strategicBriefing.whenToUse: County forums, editorial boards, and any setting where Hammer portrays 2025 petition bills as new. Pair with verified act numbers when citing enactment.
strategicBriefing.whenNotToUse: Until enrolled-act text is reviewed for a specific claim. Do not imply criminal intent or stolen elections. Avoid quoting FOIA exemption scope beyond verified statutory language.
strategicBriefing.oppositionSetup: Hammer likely argues: rules protect voters, clerks needed guardrails after 2020, transparency through official channels not ballot fishing expeditions.
strategicBriefing.kellyMessageHelp: Kelly runs the office that trains and supports counties—modernization means clear rules, funded implementation, and respect for lawful participation (in-person, absentee, initiative). Contrast: legislator adds duties; Secretary of State delivers service.
strategicBriefing.campaignAlignment: Supports SOS-as-service narrative, county partnership, voting-rights-as-practical-access, and direct-democracy respect in later sessions.
